content.title: About
content.content: Blackberries are dark purple-black, juicy fruits of thorny shrubs in the genus Rubus, widely found in temperate regions. They have a sweet and tart flavor and a slightly seedy texture. Blackberries are eaten fresh and used in jams, desserts, baked goods, smoothies, and sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Botanically, a blackberry is an aggregate fruit made of many small drupelets rather than a true berry.
Blackberries grow on thorny canes known as brambles, and wild blackberries are common in hedgerows.
Unlike raspberries, blackberries keep their core when picked.
Blackberries are among the highest-fiber fruits per serving.
They are related to raspberries and roses.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Blackberries are a rich source of fiber, which supports digestion and fullness.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C and vitamin K
items.content: These vitamins support the immune system and normal blood clotting.

items.title: Provides manganese and folate
items.content: These nutrients support metabolism and cell function.

items.title: Contains anthocyanins
items.content: These plant pigments have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Blackberries are lower in sugar than many other fruits.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some people may be allergic to blackberries or sensitive to the natural salicylates they contain.

items.title: Possible medication interactions
items.content: Blackberries contain vitamin K. People taking blood thinners should consult a healthcare professional about keeping their intake consistent.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of fiber and seeds may cause bloating in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Spoilage and wild berries
items.content: Blackberries spoil quickly, and wild berries should be washed thoroughly and picked away from roadsides and treated areas.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Blackberries can be eaten fresh, added to yogurt, oatmeal, salads, and smoothies, or baked into pies, cobblers, and muffins. They can also be cooked into jams, sauces, and syrups. Wash them gently just before eating.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Blackberries are delicate and should be refrigerated unwashed in a single layer in a breathable container and eaten within two to three days. Discard any moldy berries right away. They can be frozen on a tray and stored in a bag for longer storage.
